messages:
lucy: CI blocked release for @redwood/samplekit. publish job failed after regen produced a diff.
omar: what changed in the regen diff?
lucy: only the changelog header: generator now includes `generated-by` metadata and a timestamp like `## 1.4.5 - 2026-12-02T08:41:22Z (gen:devbox:lucy)` which flips on each run.
ci-bot: :x: publish failed for @redwood/samplekit@1.4.5 - npm ERR! 409 Conflict - document with that version already exists
keith: oh no, we also saw a semver stamp mismatch - publish pipeline expects exact version and changelog hash to be stable. This timestamp churn breaks the zero-diff gate.
dia: Are there any other diffs besides that header?
lucy: git diff shows a single hunk adding a timestamp suffix. No API surface changes.
omar: We should follow reproducible build practice: set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from `git show -s --format=%ct $COMMIT_SHA` in CI, and have the generator prefer that when present.
keith: Agree. Also, the `generated-by` bit is noisy for release branches. Maybe strip env/host info for release regen.
dia: Another wrinkle: publish-bot sees 409 and retries auth; meanwhile the sample-app e2e that depends on the new package times out because the package is already present but identical. Tests end up failing on the expectation that the registry returns a new publish event.
lucy: Proposal: 1) hotfix CI: set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and pass `--stable` to the changelog generator 2) add a prepublish guard that checks if npm 409 + published package checksum matches local artifact, treat as success 3) remove host-specific `generated-by` suffix for release branches 4) add regen-no-diff integration test in the pipeline.
omar: For (2) be careful: only treat 409-as-success if the package tarball checksum (shasum) matches what we intended to publish. We can fetch `npm view @redwood/samplekit@1.4.5 dist.shasum` and compare.
keith: Good call. That avoids masking real bad publishes.
dia: For the regen detection, let's add a small script that runs regen twice in a clean checkout and asserts `git status --porcelain` is empty. Put it in release CI as an explicit check.
lucy: I'll open PR for CI env + generator flag today. omar, can you take the prepublish checksum guard?
omar: Yup. I'll also add a debug log when we short-circuit publish due to checksum match so release notes show what happened.
keith: I'll split out the `generated-by` removal behind a `--release-mode` flag in the generator so devs still see provenance locally.
dia: And update docs / changelog spec so contributors don't hand-edit auto sections; add a lint rule to warn on edits to `### UNRELEASED` auto blocks.
lucy: One more test: add a flake guard in sample-app e2e that retries fetching the package with backoff for a short window instead of hard-failing on first miss. That reduces cascading failures from transient publish timing.
omar: I'll also make publish-bot use exponential backoff with jitter seeded from commit SHA to avoid synchronized retries.
ci-bot: Logs: https://ci.example.com/build/2860012345/logs (artifact: packages/samplekit/CHANGELOG.diff)
lucy: Thanks all. Plan: hotfix PRs for CI + generator flags + prepublish guard. Followups: lint rule and regen integration test. Tagging @devex and @eng-release for visibility. :rocket:
